title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is an altered image presented as a real photograph of real people. The original showed three students at a 2024 Lunar New Year event. The version Stanford placed on campus banners replaced one of them, Billy Ramirez, with an image of a Black woman, and made the other two look thinner. The change was made with artificial intelligence and was not disclosed.

The failure sits at the production stage of public-facing marketing material, not inside the model. Stanford's own AI policy bans using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements, and the university said both the alteration and the failure to disclose it broke that rule. Catching it would have taken a review step before the banners went up, one that compared the finished image against the original and checked it against the policy, and a disclosure if an altered image was to be used at all.

What is not established is who made the alteration, whether it was deliberate, and what consequences followed beyond the training and review Stanford said it is arranging with Residential and Dining Enterprises.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic Stanford senior studying human biology, was in a 2024 Lunar New Year photo with two other students. The university dining service posted it online the next day. Last week, Stanford used the image on campus banners. In that version, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other students were altered to look thinner. Ramirez learned about it from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated, though he also saw a comedic element.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to change the original photo. The university said its AI policy strictly bans using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and to make sure all materials are properly reviewed.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
